title: An Efficient Compute-in-Memory based Accelerator for Point-based Point Cloud Neural Networks
problem: Point-based point cloud neural networks are computationally intensive and exhibit poor performance on resource-constrained edge devices due to irregular data access patterns and high memory bandwidth requirements.
motivation: Point cloud processing is critical for 3D sensing and robotics; compute-in-memory can reduce data movement and improve energy efficiency.
method: Point-CIM accelerates point cloud processing with a reconfigurable compute-in-memory unit (a special chip that performs calculations where data is stored and can be configured for different tasks). It uses three techniques to reduce unnecessary work: skipping multiplications by zero, reorganizing 3D point data in a spatial order (Voxel-Morton-sorted Partitioning) with minimum reference points per feature channel for better compression, and storing numbers in fewer bits (Bit-level Truncation Quantization) without needing extra hardware. An optimized data arrangement loads everything to the compute array in one sequence, avoiding repeated transfers between buffer and array.
key_novelty: Point-CIM's core idea is a reconfigurable compute-in-memory architecture that accelerates point cloud neural networks by exploiting bit-level sparsity (using fewer bits per number) through feature decomposition and compression-aware optimization.
contributions: Reconfigurable CIM unit with zero-bit-skipping capability for decomposed sparse feature MAC
Voxel-Morton-sorted Partitioning (VMP) and Channel-wise Minimum base point selection for improved decomposition sparsity
Bit-level Truncation Quantization (BTQ) for lossless bit-width compression
Pre-decomposition data movement strategy reducing intermediate feature transfers
1.69-9.63× speedup, 3.11-17.32× energy efficiency improvement vs state-of-the-art
limitations: Evaluation limited to point cloud networks; applicability to other 3D processing tasks and multi-batch scenarios not discussed.
primary_theme: sparsity-exploiting CIM accelerator for point cloud networks
